verses.1: Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
verses.2: For with the judgment you pronounce, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.
verses.3: Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the plank in your own eye?
verses.4: Or how can you say to your brother, “Let me take out the speck from your eye,” when there is a plank in your own eye?
verses.5: Hypocrite, take the plank out of your own eye first, and then you will see clearly to take out the speck from your brother’s eye.
verses.6: Don’t give what is holy to dogs, and don’t throw your pearls before pigs, or they might trample them underfoot and then turn and tear you to pieces.
verses.7: Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you.
verses.8: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
verses.9: Or which of you, if your child asks for bread, will give a stone to him instead?
verses.10: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a serpent?
verses.11: If you, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
verses.12: So in everything, do to others what you would have them do to you, for this is the Law and the Prophets.
verses.13: Enter through the narrow gate, for the gate is wide and the road is broad that leads to destruction, and there are many who enter through it.
verses.14: For the gate is narrow and the road is hard that leads to life, and few are those who find it.
verses.15: Watch out for false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
verses.16: You will recognize them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
verses.17: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but the bad tree bears bad fruit.
verses.18: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a bad tree bear good fruit.
verses.19: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
verses.20: So you will recognize them by their fruits.
verses.21: Not everyone who says to me, “Lord, Lord,” will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
verses.22: On that day many will say to me, “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name perform many miracles?”
verses.23: Then I will declare to them, “I never knew you. Go away from me, you workers of lawlessness.”
verses.24: Therefore, everyone who hears these words of mine and puts them into practice is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
verses.25: The rain came down, the rivers rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house, but it did not fall because it had been founded on the rock.
verses.26: Everyone who hears these words of mine but does not put them into practice is like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
verses.27: The rain came down, the rivers rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell—and its fall was great.
verses.28: Now when Jesus finished these words, the crowds were astonished at his teaching,
verses.29: for he was teaching them with authority, and not like their scribes.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: “serpent” is used for ὄφις, which can be a literal snake or symbolic of something harmful.
- v. 12: The phrase “this is the Law and the Prophets” reflects the Jewish understanding of Scripture as encapsulated in these two divisions.
- v. 23: “workers of lawlessness” translates ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν, where ἀνομία (anomia) refers to lawlessness or disregard for divine law.
- v. 24–27: The parable of the wise and foolish builders is rendered to preserve the contrast and the symbolic nature of the foundation materials.
